issue.title: S2 · Devices can't impersonate each other
issue.body:
### Summary
Anyone can send messages "from B" and swap B's key (T-S1). Fix: a device's id is the first 128 bits of SHA-256(public key) in base64url (22 characters), with a format check in `isDevId`. All setup after the key is sealed: the WebRTC offer carries the DTLS fingerprint, so sealing it is what stops the direct-link hijack.
### Acceptance (the attack fails)
A key that doesn't hash to its id is dropped. A forged "from B" setup from a third browser is dropped and A links to the real B. Edge: B leaves and rejoins with a new key and still connects. Scope: device messages only. Room messages go with S1.1 and S1.4. Ids not in the room are #21.

### Update (PR #50, design review)
- A device has two key pairs: encryption (ECDH P-256) and signing (ECDSA P-256). Its id is the first 128 bits of the SHA-256 of **both** public keys, so nobody can attach their own signing key to another device's id (ARCHITECTURE.md, Keys).
- Room messages are signed with the ECDSA key and checked against the key bound to the id. No signed message is accepted until the keys match the id.
- A colour and three emoji made from the id are shown next to each name, as a visual aid only.
